entries.status: No EU-level schedule or class. EU legislation does not establish classes of narcotic or psychotropic substances; Member States classify drugs according to the 1961, 1971 and 1988 UN Conventions. The Framework Decision on illicit drug trafficking defines 'drug' as any substance covered by the 1961 Single Convention (as amended by the 1972 Protocol) or by the 1971 Convention, or listed in its Annex.

Amharic text: 'ናርኮቲክ መድኃኒት' (narcotic medicine), controlled under 'የናርኮቲክ መድኃኒቶች ስምምነት' (the narcotic drugs convention)

entries.checked_by: AI reader W2 (two WebFetch readings compared by script)
entries.note: The site's UN layer places Heroin (diacetylmorphine) in Schedules I and IV of the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961. Ethiopia is a party to the Single Convention, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol (1994-10-11; unamended Convention by accession 1965-04-29), per the site's UN Treaty Collection data. Not named in any Ethiopian list read (National List of May 2017, Parts I-IV and Annex forms; EFDA tramadol notice; Directive No. 1121/2025, readable part). The Proclamation fixes no date and no schedule numbers for the reference; whether it reaches substances scheduled internationally after 28 February 2019 is unsettled (see 'unsettled'). Art. 2(11) speaks of 'a medicine' (Amharic መድኃኒት); whether it reaches a narcotic drug that is not used as a medicine is a question of interpretation (see 'unsettled').
